prompt.zh-TW: 上方表格是雲梯軟體的 RD intensity：今年營收 {{money:vars.revenue}}，研究發展費用 {{money:vars.rdExpense}}。另一家海鷗五金行的 RD intensity 只有 {{percent:vars.rdHardware}}。下列哪一個解讀最合理？
prompt.en: The table above shows Cloud Ladder Software’s R&D intensity: revenue of {{money:vars.revenue}} this year and research and development expense of {{money:vars.rdExpense}}. Seagull Hardware’s R&D intensity is only {{percent:vars.rdHardware}}. Which reading is the most reasonable?

text.zh-TW: 雲梯投入研發的比例高，符合軟體業的特性，不能和五金行直接比
text.en: Cloud Ladder puts a high share of revenue into research, as a software firm would, and cannot be ranked directly against a hardware shop

feedback.zh-TW: 答對了。RD intensity 說的是研發在生意裡的分量，不同產業的合理區間差很多，比較要找同業。
feedback.en: Correct. R&D intensity shows how much research weighs in the business; sensible ranges differ widely by industry, so comparisons belong within the same sector.

text.zh-TW: 海鷗經營得比較好，因為研發花得少，省下的都是利潤
text.en: Seagull is better run, because it spends less on research and the savings are all profit

feedback.zh-TW: 研發是為了未來的營收，不只是今天的費用。五金行本來就不需要太多研發，軟體公司砍研發反而可能砍掉明年的產品；RD intensity 沒有「越低越好」這回事。
feedback.en: Research is spent for future revenue, not just today’s expense. A hardware shop naturally needs little research, while a software firm that cuts research may be cutting next year’s products; there is no ‘lower is better’ rule for R&D intensity.

text.zh-TW: 雲梯的研發費用金額一定比海鷗多，因為比例比較高
text.en: Cloud Ladder’s research spending must be larger in absolute terms than Seagull’s, because its share is higher

feedback.zh-TW: RD intensity 是比例，不是金額。營收很大的五金連鎖，即使比例低，研發的金額也可能比一家小軟體公司多；要比金額得回到損益表。
feedback.en: R&D intensity is a share, not an amount. A hardware chain with very large revenue could spend more on research in absolute terms than a small software firm despite its low share; for amounts, go back to the income statement.

explanation.zh-TW: {{option:o_z12f}}。RD intensity ＝ 研究發展費用 ÷ 營收 ＝ {{money:vars.rdExpense}} ÷ {{money:vars.revenue}}，研發費用在銷管費用裡。它回答的是「這家公司的生意有多依賴研發」，答案和產業特性綁在一起，所以高低本身沒有好壞，跨產業比較也沒有意義；要看的是同業之間的差距與自己的趨勢。
explanation.en: {{option:o_z12f}}. R&D intensity = research and development expense ÷ revenue = {{money:vars.rdExpense}} ÷ {{money:vars.revenue}}, with research costs sitting within distribution costs and administrative expenses. It answers ‘how much does this business depend on research’, and the answer is tied to the industry, so a high or low figure is neither good nor bad in itself and comparing across industries means little; what matters is the gap against peers and the company’s own trend.
